scenario: Adopt Lintwise as a required pre-merge check (eight engineers)

motion.text: The team adopts Lintwise, an automated code-quality checker, as a required pre-merge check on every repository.

research: Marcus: Run Lintwise in parallel with the existing CI build on a representative branch set of our monorepo (including a 40+ file PR); record median wall-clock delta, worst-case tail latency, and queue-depth impact at peak merge windows. Bring the numbers to the next meeting.

Sana: Check Lintwise's supported-language list for SQL; run it against a sample of our pipeline .sql files to confirm it actually parses them (not silently skips) and measure false-positive rate on stored-procedure patterns. Bring coverage and noise numbers to the next meeting.

chairQuestions.topic: Measured runtime delta of Lintwise with a scoped high-severity ruleset versus the default full rulebook on a comparable codebase
chairQuestions.experience_sought: Priya ran Lintwise for six months on a prior team. We need the concrete wall-clock numbers: was the ~4-minute figure with the default rulebook, and what did the runtime drop to after she scoped to high-severity checks? Also, was that measured on a monorepo of similar scale or a smaller repo?

chairQuestions.topic: Specific false-positive instances encountered on the React project and how each was resolved
chairQuestions.experience_sought: Tom ran Lintwise on a small React project and flagged issues. We need the factual record: what were the false positives (rule names, file types), how many per PR on average, and what resolution did he use—inline suppression comment, config exclusion, or rule disable?
